new_entities.name: Cognitive decline and dementia prevention
new_entities.description: Longitudinal cognitive decline or progression to dementia in older adults.

edges.population: older adults with memory complaints, normal cognition, mild cognitive impairment, or established dementia
edges.mechanism: Ginkgo is proposed to combine mild vascular, antioxidant, and platelet-related effects that could theoretically support cerebral perfusion and neuronal resilience. In prevention settings, that broad mechanism has not translated into convincing long-term reduction in incident dementia, even though some shorter treatment trials in symptomatic dementia populations have shown modest cognitive benefits.
edges.summary: Ginkgo biloba at 240 mg daily does not have strong evidence as a dementia-prevention strategy, despite some positive treatment-era dementia trials. The cleanest long-term randomized studies are largely null for preventing Alzheimer disease or slowing cognitive decline, which is why the overall edge stays mixed rather than clearly beneficial.
edges.caveats: This edge blends two related but different questions: symptom treatment in established dementia and true prevention in at-risk elders. A short-term benefit on dementia scales should not be confused with proof that ginkgo prevents future decline or incident Alzheimer disease.
